parsed.why: State courts repeatedly enjoin anti-trans laws, but hostile legislature, RFRA-style religious exemption, and unresolved 2026 sex-definition law leave local exposure; national border, facilities and custody rules still apply.

Bathroom-bounty law creates private enforcement, criminal/civil penalties, and invalidates IDs in public buildings including airports; state-imposed universal exposure with no working remedy, on top of the restrictive national regime.
Strong state nondiscrimination, hate-crime, panic-defence repeal and shield laws, but these are mostly resident-facing and cannot offset the national border, facilities and custody exposure.
Low-risk state with codified gender-identity protections, explicit hate-crime coverage and panic-defence ban, but absent X-marker confirmation and national framework still govern visitor exposure.

Most-protective state with shield laws and broad insurance coverage, but documented birth-sex prison transfer of a trans woman and pending ballot initiatives temper it; national border and custody rules remain.
